title: Cartesian fibration over a groupoid completion
statement: Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Inner fibration has the inner-horn lifting meaning of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. In this statement a Cartesian fibration $p:X\to Y$ means an inner fibration admitting a lift $x'\to x$ of every arrow $y'\to p(x)$ with specified target, such that for every $z\in X$ the square $\operatorname{Map}_X(z,x')\to\operatorname{Map}_X(z,x)$ over $\operatorname{Map}_Y(pz,y')\to\operatorname{Map}_Y(pz,px)$ is a homotopy pullback. For a small infinity-category $W$, choose a Kan fibrant replacement $\eta:W\to\kappa W$ in the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]: $\kappa W$ is a Kan complex and $\eta$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Such a replacement exists in the same universe; it is called the groupoid completion. Let $\pi:\mathcal F\to\kappa W$ be a Cartesian fibration and form the pullback $\mathcal F'=W\times_{\kappa W}\mathcal F$ in infinity-categories. Then restriction along $\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F$ identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal F,\mathcal T)$ with the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal F',\mathcal T)$ on functors carrying every arrow whose image in $\mathcal F$ is an equivalence to an equivalence, including all mapping spaces, for every target infinity-category $\mathcal T$ in a sufficiently large universe.
